newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares seen stopping for breath after rally.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares seen stopping for breath after rally.

text.p: The Belgian share market, which on Thursday broke through resistance to set its third new year high in three days, is expected to pause for breath on Friday after its rampant week, traders said.
Some undermining is also due from a faltering Wall Street, they added.
The BEL-20 index, which had been holding cautious gains for most of the day, took heart from opening Wall Street gains to edge above resistance at 1,800 points for the first time ever.
It spurted nearly 30 points more as an estimated one billion francs of buying orders hit the market in the last minute.
"There was a lot of index buying at the close. It was pushed to unrealistic levels," one trader said.

The BEL-20 closed at a record high of 1,829.85 points, up 39.33 points or 2.20 percent. There were 19 gainers and one loser. Total market volume was 4.9 billion francs, roughly double the volume of an averagely busy day in Belgium.
There was no immediate explanation of who had been tweaking the market or why.
Technically there is now clear blue sky above the index, although traders pointed out that it tended not to be overly influenced by technical factors.
"If the Dow Jones comes down, then so will we," one trader remarked.
The banking sector had the best of the day.
Generale Bank recovered from earlier losses to clock up gains of 400 francs at 11,150. BBL hit a new year high of 6,600 francs, up 300. Kredietbank added 250 francs to 10,450.
Elsewhere, steel cord and wire maker Bekaert benefitted from an upgrading to buy from hold by BBL to add 350 francs at 24,500.
